subject: SIG questionnaire: VPC peering evidence, egress IPs and private endpoint behavior
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG: Need VPC peering evidence + allowlist for production ingress

Hi Karthik,

We're working through Acme's SIG and the security team has a couple of outstanding asks before they approve production traffic:

- Confirm the egress IPs/redwood-owned ranges we should allow for outbound traffic from your peered VPCs (CSV preferred).
- Provide a short network diagram showing VPC peering / private endpoint topology for our production tenant.
- Clarify whether private endpoints are sticky or ephemeral per session, and how persistent connections are handled (we need to ensure our NAT/IDS rules won't drop traffic).

Can you point me to the artifacts or send a single package we can attach to the SIG? The security reviewer wants this by COB Wednesday 20-May if possible.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Reynolds
Security Lead, Acme Cloud Platforms
security@acme-corp.com

--
Attachment request: topology diagram, egress IP list, short operational note on private endpoints (1 page)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG: Need VPC peering evidence + allowlist for production ingress

Tom —

Thanks for the clear asks. I've pulled together the materials below and attached the files you requested. Short answers up front:

- Egress IPs: we publish a stable egress pool for Dedicated and Private deployments. For your production tenant we've reserved the CIDR ranges in the attached egress_ip_list.csv (these are the NAT egress addresses you can allow).
- Diagram: attached redwood_vpc_peering_topology.png shows the peering, private endpoint (PrivateLink-style) placements, and the optional transit NAT for cross-AZ failover.
- Private endpoint behavior: Private endpoints themselves are static network interfaces (ENIs) created in your VPC; the service-side connections are backed by a transient compute fleet. Because we maintain a stable endpoint IP on the customer VPC side, your IDS/NAT rules should target the endpoint's ENI; the backend pod/processes can be scaled without changing that endpoint. See private_endpoint_nics.txt for the technical notes.

Attachments included: redwood_vpc_peering_topology.png; egress_ip_list.csv; private_endpoint_nics.txt; also a filled SIG checklist PDF (sig-complete-answers.pdf).

CC'ing Marissa for account sign-off and Rishi for any deeper infra details you might want. If you prefer, we can provide a signed attestation packet for procurement/legal.

Next steps: please confirm whether you need the single IP addresses or CIDR ranges expanded to include our load balancer egress (we can provide both).

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

--
